dashboard.label: Cross-App Agentic Normalization
dashboard.description: Phase 6 teaching module — heterogeneous agentic telemetry (OTel GenAI, vendor-sim, third-party sim) normalized to one CIM-style field set. Agentic apps will never agree on a native schema; Splunk's value is normalizing them into one framework-mappable model.

panel.title: Lesson — Why Splunk for agentic AI security

html.p: Real environments run multiple agentic stacks with incompatible field names. This lab ships three deliberate conventions:

ul.li: otel:agentic:json — primary OTel GenAI pipeline (gen_ai.usage.input_tokens, acme_output_guard.action)

html.p: Normalization lives in props.conf calculated fields (norm_*) — not per-dashboard coalesce() chains. One query below works across all three.

search.query: `acme_agentic_all_sources` $global_time$ | eval source_app=case(sourcetype="otel:agentic:json", "primary_otel", sourcetype="acme:agentic:vendorsim:json", "vendor_sim", sourcetype="acme:agentic:thirdparty:json", "third_party", 1=1, "other") | head 15 | table _time source_app sourcetype gen_ai.agent.name agent.id agent_name agent_id acme_output_guard.action policy_action policy_result threat_label gen_ai.usage.input_tokens gen_ai_input_tokens token_count_in

panel.title: Normalized view — same query, all sources

search.query: `acme_agentic_all_sources` $global_time$ | eval source_app=case(sourcetype="otel:agentic:json", "primary_otel", sourcetype="acme:agentic:vendorsim:json", "vendor_sim", sourcetype="acme:agentic:thirdparty:json", "third_party", 1=1, "other") | stats count avg(norm_input_tokens) AS avg_in avg(norm_output_tokens) AS avg_out values(norm_action) AS actions by source_app norm_agent_identity norm_signature | sort source_app -count

panel.title: Normalization coverage — attestation gap by source

search.query: `acme_agentic_all_sources` $global_time$ | eval source_app=case(sourcetype="otel:agentic:json", "primary_otel", sourcetype="acme:agentic:vendorsim:json", "vendor_sim", sourcetype="acme:agentic:thirdparty:json", "third_party", 1=1, "other") | stats count sum(norm_mapped) AS mapped by source_app | eval coverage_pct=round(100*mapped/count,1) | table source_app count mapped coverage_pct
